items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: I still think those were two of the best sides out of New Orleans in the 20s

ctx.x: You were marvelous then. I mean, it went to that extreme with some people. Yeah. I'm sure it depended on who said it. Yes, and people. Well, I can remember playing with the music, and I was like, I'm sure it was a little bit of colorless to colorless distorted the people we thought of as being Jim Crow. It certainly influenced me so that I, well, I sometimes would not bother to go listen to white bands that I later learned to enjoy, even though I always was arguing with people to listen to both, and I'd make, I…
I'll tell you, that was, Byerstoffer was, I think they only got about four sides out of, two sides? Two. And I still think those were two of the best sides out of New Orleans in the 20s that I'd
ever run across. I always regretted that I never interviewed him, I knew him. Was he? Oh. And he came back, do you remember? No, I don't. He even played at the famous store for a little while.
